reviews.author: Sue
reviews.text:
This electrical wholesaler also sells on eBay.  I was informed that my order had been cancelled as the item was out of stock or damaged.  A few minutes later I checked and they had simply raised the price and continued to sell the item, this is completely against eBay rules.  After defending their actions vigorously they did eventually offer to sell at the original price ('do you want us to sell at a loss').  I declined their offer, as I wouldn't want to have to deal with them if there was a problem with the item.

Update: following the strange response below (I may have been forthright, but certainly wasn't abusive, and reported their eventual offer to follow through in my review), I have confirmed with eBay that the action of selling an item, cancelling the order and then immediately raising the price is strictly against their rules and they are investigating this seller.

I found the attitude of both the people I spoke to very strange, it was if they thought I was the one that had done something wrong, not them.  eBay is a retail market, not a wholesale one, in which this wholesale company has chosen to participate and as such it needs to understand the rules of the retail market.  Given that they only have 13 different items listed on eBay, it shouldn't be hard to comply.  eBay does not allow buyers whose orders are cancelled to leave feedback, which in my case would certainly have affected their 100% feedback.
